create.name: Jeff Warren
create.bio:
Jeff Warren is a Canadian meditation teacher and writer who began as a journalist, producing radio for CBC programmes such as The Current and Ideas and writing about the science of the mind for magazines and newspapers. His first book, The Head Trip, tours the different states of consciousness a person passes through in a single day and night. He has trained with the American teacher Shinzen Young since 2008, and in 2011 he started the Consciousness Explorers Club, a non-profit meditation community in Toronto that welcomes many styles of practice.

He teaches a small set of attention skills, chiefly concentration, clarity and equanimity, and adapts the technique to each person rather than the other way round. His manner is informal and very funny, and he is open about being neurodivergent himself. With Dan Harris and Carlye Adler he wrote Meditation for Fidgety Skeptics, and many of his guided sessions live on the Calm and Happier apps. Each Sunday evening he hosts The Do Nothing Project, a free livestreamed sit, and he runs Home Base, a low-cost online community on Substack. He also leads retreats at Omega Institute, where he co-hosts the yearly Meditation Party, and at centres in California, North Carolina and British Columbia.

books.title: Meditation for Fidgety Skeptics: A 10% Happier How-to Book
books.author: Dan Harris, Jeff Warren, Carlye Adler
books.description: Harris and Warren take a bus across the United States to meet people who have given up on sitting practice, and answer their objections one at a time. Chapters end with brief practices meant to slot into ordinary routines.

books.title: The Head Trip: Adventures on the Wheel of Consciousness
books.author: Jeff Warren
books.description: A science writer's tour of the states the mind moves through over twenty-four hours, from dreaming and the half-awake hypnagogic edge to trance, flow and meditation. He tries each one out himself alongside interviews with researchers.

courses.title: Being Human Takes Practice (Omega Institute)
courses.description: A weekend meditation retreat on Omega's Rhinebeck campus for beginners and sceptics as much as seasoned sitters. He guides a range of techniques so that each person can find what suits them, with sharing, discussion and time outdoors.

courses.title: Meditation Party (Omega Institute)
courses.description: A large, sociable three-day retreat at Omega co-led with Dan Harris and Sebene Selassie. Plenty of sitting from three different angles, plus movement, naps and conversation; it is not a silent retreat.

courses.title: Where Meditation Leads (Toronto and online)
courses.description: A three-hour afternoon of guided practice and open discussion at a Toronto library, also streamed on Zoom, raising funds for the Consciousness Explorers Club. Entry is on a sliding scale.

courses.title: Meditation and Mystery (Big Bear Retreat Center)
courses.description: A five-day retreat in the mountains of Southern California on the core skills of meditation and where long practice can lead. Quiet periods sit alongside group sharing, with a mostly silent option for those who want it.
courses.price: From $760 USD (triple room, shared bath; meals and programme included)

courses.title: Meditation, Movement, Mystery (Hollyhock)
courses.description: A loosely structured retreat on Cortes Island, British Columbia, moving between seated practice, movement, ceremony and time to relate, ending with an evening dance. Booking is through Hollyhock.

courses.title: Home Base
courses.description: His online practice community on Substack: a weekly piece of writing paired with a new guided meditation, plus live hangouts. Much of it is free, with extra meditations for paying members.
courses.price: Free, or $12 USD a month / $80 USD a year

courses.title: The Elements of Meditation
courses.description: A short self-paced video course that sets out the main families of technique and what each one trains, with notes on common sticking points. Aimed at newcomers who feel lost among the options.

courses.title: 1:1 Practice Accelerator
courses.description: Three one-hour private sessions over a month for people who already practise and want to work through sticking points, ending with a guided recording made for them. Places are by application.

free_resources.title: The Do Nothing Project
free_resources.description: A free live meditation every Sunday at 8pm Eastern, with a few words of welcome and a minimal 25-minute sit that people from many countries join. Past sessions are archived on his YouTube channel.

free_resources.title: Community Practice Activation Kit
free_resources.description: A free guide to starting a small peer-led meditation group with friends or colleagues, covering format, roles and simple scripts.

free_resources.title: The Junior Cult Leader's Guide to Beginner Meditation
free_resources.description: A free, light-hearted starter post on Home Base for people new to sitting, with a short guided practice to go with it.

free_resources.title: Welcome Home (guided meditation)
free_resources.description: An open-access guided meditation and short reflection from Home Base, a gentle way to try his style before subscribing.

sprint.tier_evidence: Instagram 29K followers (og:description of instagram.com/_jeffwarren_, 31 Oct 2026); YouTube 25.1K subscribers (channel header row next to @JeffWarrenMeditation, 31 Oct 2026); no other own accounts linked from his site → ~54k total → local_hero
flags: Overlap in the sprint: co-leads Omega's 'Meditation Party' (same eomega URL) with Dan Harris (dan-harris.json) and Sebene Selassie (skipped); 'Meditation for Fidgety Skeptics' is listed on both his plan and Dan Harris's.
No email published ('I don't manage email myself'); contact form at jeffwarren.org/contact, plus a separate speaking inquiry form.

His site frames meditation around stress, grief, ADHD and mental health (he is open about being ADHD and bipolar); the bio says only that he is neurodivergent, and condition-framed events were left out. A human may want to confirm the fit.

Availability set to worldwide: he founded the Toronto-based Consciousness Explorers Club but calls the Toronto event a 'rare in-person' one; teaching is mostly online and at retreat centres in the US and Canada.
Tier: Instagram + YouTube ~54k → local_hero; his guided meditations on Calm and Happier reach far more people, and his co-authored book was a bestseller; no override applied.
Hollyhock (in the future hubs queue, §18.7) and Big Bear also host his retreats; offering URLs are his own event pages, which link to the centres' booking pages.
left_out: Retreat 'Meditate, Relate and Creatively Self-Regulate: A Retreat for Neurodivergent Humans' (July 2026): past and condition-framed.
